newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.N. condemns Croat jailing of Bosnian Serbs.
newsitem.headline: U.N. condemns Croat jailing of Bosnian Serbs.

text.p: The United Nations on Thursday condemned as little more than hostage-taking the jailing by Bosnian Croats of four Bosnian Serbs for alleged spying.

"Basically they (the Serb civilians) were taken as hostages for the exchange of two HVO (Bosnian Croat militia) soldiers," Alex Ivanko, spokesman for the U.N.'s International Police Task Force (IPTF), told reporters in the capital Sarajevo.

Ivanko said Peter Fitzgerald, Commissioner of the IPTF, which monitors local police work and human rights standards in post-war Bosnia, planned to write to Bosnian Croat authorities demanding the unconditional release of the four Serbs.
The men were jailed for 27 days in Croat-controlled northern Bosnia for allegedly spying on a Croat militia base, the U.N. said.

The four were sentenced on Wednesday in the northeastern town of Orasje a day after being detained by the HVO while crossing Croat-held territory between the Bosnian Serb towns of Bijeljina and Bosanski Brod in the ethnically-divided country.
Two other Serbs were freed after questioning.
The IPTF said the Serbs related how they were detained after losing their way in dense fog.

"They took the road to (Croat-controlled) Odzak. Somewhere near Donja Dubica they stopped a car to check their map. They met HVO (Croat militia) soldiers who ordered the Serbs to follow them," IPTF spokesman Andrea Angeli said.
The Serbs' cars and vehicles were checked at a nearby Croat camp and nothing illegal was found but the Croats released only two Serbs after interrogation, Angeli told Reuters.
"IPTF was able to see them (jailed Serbs) yesterday afternoon and they are okay," said Angeli.
The Serbs told the U.N. police they were from the southern town of Trebinje at the other end of Bosnia.
